cells.value: 1. Claude Code (and Claude Desktop's local config)

Install pinned: claude plugin marketplace add https://github.com/ComposioHQ/composio-plugin-cc.git#v0.2.4, then install composio@composio. The plugin's own daily self-update then resolves to the same tag (last result: current). Version 0.2.4 installed.

Every MCP call and every Bash command that mentions composio goes through ~/.agents/tools/guards/composio_guard.py (agents-home; the stricter version 527f1e7 since 2026-10-03). It stops spend, sends to clients or anyone outside increaseroas.com, deletes, DNS changes, deploys and security changes (Tailscale policy, keys, users and devices) until Alex says yes in chat. There is no stored guard code: each stop prints a one-time code (CG-XXXX), one per delete, and Alex approves by typing yes to a message that names the code. A yes can't release a rule denial, because the call itself is wrong: no login named on a toolkit with more than one login, a payload file the guard can't read at a literal path, or a path into ~/Library/Containers or Group Containers. The call has to be corrected (composio card, Guard). A deny holds even in bypass mode.

herdr's agent-state hook. Optional; what herdr is for is gap G04.

Four hooks run ~/.agents/tools/guards/chat_guard.py (agents-home), each with a 20-second limit. Chat size never blocks: at 20 MB it saves a handoff snapshot and asks Alex once, fresh chat or keep going, then again every +15 MB. Memory acts only near the limit (under 10% available, or macOS says critical): no new agents until it recovers, and the biggest command this chat started (over 2 GiB) is stopped; no memory notes above that. Every agent prompt gets one memory-safe line (no whole-home scans; stream files over 50 MB). Why: the 2026-10-02 20:46 out-of-memory crash, caused by an agent's whole-home scan (8.69 GiB). Turn off: remove the chat_guard.py entries.
Matches (live since 2026-10-02 21:22; the script is the round-2 file of 22:27)
